A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same flatness–representation study and retain matching CIFAR-10 experiments. All six pages of v1 and seventeen pages of v2 support comparison, including v2's Appendices A–E. V1 has no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original VGG10 experiments on two CIFAR-10 classes, including learning-rate and batch-size sweeps and analyses of held-out and misclassified samples (Figures 1–3).

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds FashionMNIST experiments, empirical bound-tightness checks, and correlations across trained networks (Appendices D–E).

M1.justification: The stated quadratic loss gains a factor of 1/2 in v2's mathematical setup, aligning its normalization with the Hessian identity. This is a limited change to the reported loss formulation; the PDFs do not establish altered training implementations. The underlying feedforward-network and SGD procedure remains.

E1.justification: V2 adds FashionMNIST classification alongside the retained two-class CIFAR-10 experiments (Section 4.1; Appendices D–E). This extends dataset coverage within image classification without introducing another task family.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks a proposed training algorithm against competing methods. V2's additional MLP architecture, representation metrics, and intermediate bounds support experimental and theoretical analyses; they do not add an evaluated baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: V2 adds MLS measurements, four-layer MLP experiments, and endpoint comparisons across 20 differently configured or initialized networks per architecture. Figures 1–2 also change the stated sharpness quantity from Equation (3) to its square root, without establishing reruns. The original CIFAR-10 sampling and hyperparameter sweeps remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's hyperparameter sweeps and misclassification analyses, Appendix D tests the slack introduced by successive bound relaxations and compares representation metrics with sharpness and test loss. Appendix E extends the learning-rate and batch-size sensitivity analyses to MLPs on FashionMNIST.

E5.justification: V2 introduces Pearson correlation estimation for ensembles of 20 networks (Figures D.5–D.6). The retained experiment still reports five random initializations; the new ensembles vary hyperparameters as well as initialization and do not establish increased repetitions under fixed settings. Confidence intervals and significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: The original CIFAR-10 training trends are retained, while v2 adds MLP trajectories and quantitative correlation and tightness results. MLS correlates with sharpness at 0.90 for VGG10 and 0.99 for MLPs (Figures D.5–D.6). Figure D.6 additionally reports a negative correlation of -0.93 between MLS and bound D.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the averaged volume bound by adding n^{max(N/2-1,0)} in Equation (12), absent from v1's Equation (13). It adds an approximate-interpolation lemma, spectral-norm inequalities, the MLS definition and bound, proofs, and equality-condition analysis (Appendices A–D). V1's perturbative argument for SGD minimizing sharpness is removed.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion expand the contributions beyond the retained volume–sharpness connection to include MLS, claimed reparametrization-invariant bounds, correlations with test loss, and explanations for conflicting sharpness–generalization findings. These substantially broaden the paper's principal scientific claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains how nonuniform Jacobian spectra and vanishing eigenvalues can loosen volume bounds, motivating MLS. Appendix D interprets the different behavior of partial and full sharpness bounds and relates their looseness to network structure and mixed generalization findings. These explanations substantially extend v1's discussion of additional compression mechanisms.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly specifies k=2 for G, identifies the added MLPs as four-layer networks, and provides their SGD learning rates and batch sizes (Figures E.7–E.8). These are limited documentation additions; complete architecture specifications, hardware information, and code-access instructions remain absent.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around reparametrization and conflicting sharpness–generalization findings, adding Dinh, Andriushchenko, Wen, and several linear-model studies (Introduction; Appendix D.3). V1's separate entropy discussion and its Gabrié and Wickstrøm references are removed. The foundational connection to Ma and Ying remains.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the narrative into numbered sections and metric-specific theory subsections, moves the local-dimensionality formalism out of the experiments, and substantially rewrites the contribution statement and conclusion. Structured proof and analysis appendices replace the earlier compact presentation, although much background and experimental prose remains.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a single-column layout, resizes and relocates the original figures, and adds five figures covering bounds, correlation matrices, and MLP trajectories. Figure 3 changes from six panels in two rows to five panels in one row, but its caption still lists the removed training-loss panel.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs a substantive weakness in the central volume bound and adds proofs, direct tests of bound looseness, and quantitative connections to test loss. These changes substantially strengthen mathematical support and empirical scrutiny beyond v1's training trajectories. The new reparametrization-invariance claim remains insufficiently justified, and Figure 3 has a stale caption, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the central gains.
